answer: Invariant: identity earns weight only after surviving one market nadir bonded to a distinct site. Two conditions enforce it: registration needs a fresh sensor plume hash from a local grove, so one operator cannot mint thousands of IDs from one location without duplicate hardware; stake stays locked through a full drawdown, slashing clones that die early, weight vesting only after the trough. Bulk sybils pay real hardware plus real time, pushing marginal identity cost above marginal reward.
